Description M5Stack Cardputer-Adv: A Portable ESP32-S3 Computer The M5Stack Cardputer-Adv is a compact, programmable ESP32-S3 computer with an integrated keyboard and display. Powered by the Stamp-S3A module with an ESP32-S3FN8 processor and 8MB Flash, it combines a 56-key keyboard, a 1.14-inch colour LCD, onboard audio and a BMI270 motion sensor in a card-sized device. Its built-in input, display and expansion interfaces make it suitable for embedded programming, interactive prototypes, portable control interfaces and IoT projects. The current version features a 1500mAh rechargeable battery, a magnetic base and LEGO-compatible mounting holes. Features ESP32-S3 processor: Dual-core Xtensa LX7 processor running at up to 240MHz, with 8MB Flash. Integrated keyboard and display: A 56-key keyboard and a 1.14-inch, 240 × 135 LCD provide local input and visual output for your applications. Onboard audio: An ES8311 audio codec, MEMS microphone, NS4150B amplifier and 1W speaker support audio input and output. A 3.5mm audio output jack allows connection to external headphones or speakers. Motion sensing: The BMI270 six-axis IMU supports projects involving movement, orientation and motion-based interaction. Expansion and storage: An HY2.0-4P Grove port, EXT 2.54-14P expansion bus and microSD card slot provide options for peripherals and additional storage. Wireless and infrared: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and an infrared emitter support compatible communication and control projects. Portable power and mounting: A 1500mAh rechargeable battery, independent power switch, magnetic base and LEGO-compatible mounting holes support portable and mounted builds. Specifications These Cardputer Adv specs describe the current hardware version. Check the official documentation linked below before designing peripherals. Compared with a loose single-board-computer setup, the reComputer R1114-10 gives engineers a ready-to-integrate enclosure, protected power input, watchdog, RTC, ATECC608A security chip and industrial I/O. It is well suited for smart-building control, factory data acquisition, energy monitoring, fleet equipment gateways and local AIoT projects where a reliable Raspberry Pi IoT Gateway needs to bridge field devices and cloud services.
